Hi all, I work in ICU and I'm posting this because the police warning from Neighbourhood Policing (Levenshulme) from the 6th is getting buried. It matters too much for that. Please read it properly, and please share it, not just like it.

Blue tablets are being sold as diazepam or Xanax. Some of them have nitazenes in them. Nitazenes are synthetic opioids and can be far stronger than heroin. You can't tell what's in a pill by looking at it, so anyone who has taken one of these could be at risk.

The signs to look for are extreme drowsiness, pinpoint pupils, slow or noisy breathing, and blue lips. If you see any of these, do this:

Ring 999 straight away. Don't wait to see whether it wears off.

Don't put them to bed to sleep it off. Breathing can slow or stop while someone is asleep, and that's how people die from this. If they're breathing, put them in the recovery position and stay with them. If they stop breathing, start CPR and keep going until help arrives.

Don't let worry about getting into trouble stop you ringing. The police have said their priority is preserving life. Scared kids don't ring for help, and that's the whole problem.

Naloxone nasal spray can reverse an opioid overdose. Brightpath drug and alcohol service is on Stockport Road, next to the launderette. They give out free naloxone kits, anyone can ask, and you don't need to give a name. The training takes about ten minutes. They're open Monday to Friday 10 till 4, and Thursdays until 7. Naloxone doesn't replace calling 999, though. It can wear off, and the person still needs an ambulance.

Parents, please talk to your kids this week, not after half term or whenever. I sat down with my 14 year old over his tea last night. He rolled his eyes, but he listened, and he asked what pinpoint pupils meant, so it went in. Ask them what they'd do if a mate went quiet at a party. Tell them they can ring you from anywhere, any time, and you won't go off at them for it.

And can we stop slagging the kids off in the other thread? It helps nobody. Some of them are scared, and being shamed makes them less likely to ring for help next time. Admin has asked for no naming and no guessing, and I'd add: be kind.

Please share this in your own group chats, your kids' year groups, and anywhere else people with teenagers are. Thanks.
